requirements.text: All components submitted for approval shall bear the trade name or mark of the manufacturer and the type.
All non-metallic components submitted for approval shall also bear the manufacturing month and year.
The marking of the components submitted for approval (trade name or mark, type, and for non-metallic components also manufacturing month and year) shall be clearly legible and indelible.
All equipment shall have a space large enough to accommodate the approval mark including the classification of the component (see Annex 2A).
In case of components of Class 0, the space on the equipment shall be large enough to accommodate also the working pressure (WP).
In the case of limited space for the approval mark(s), other means of identification that link it to the approval mark shall be provided on the equipment.
Every container shall bear a marking plate, welded to it, with the data listed in items (a) to (h) of paragraph 4.3, clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear a serial number, clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the capacity in litres, clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the marking "LPG", clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the test pressure [kPa], clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the wording: "maximum degree of filling: 80 %", clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the year and month of approval (e.g. 99/01), clearly legible and indelible.
The marking plate welded to every container shall bear the approval mark according to paragraph 5.4, clearly legible and indelible.

In addition to the markings required by paragraphs 4.1. and 4.2., one of the additional marks "H1", "H2" or "H3" shall be used for remotely controlled service valves and remotely controlled shut-off valves which comply respectively with paragraph 4.7. of Annex 3 or with paragraph 1.7. of Annex 7.

There shall be affixed, conspicuously and in the space referred to in paragraph 4.2., to all equipment conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, in addition to the mark prescribed in paragraphs 4.1. and 4.3., an international approval mark consisting of the elements in paragraphs 5.4.1. and 5.4.2.
The international approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The international approval mark shall include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 5.4.1.

The approval number in the approval mark shall consist of the component type approval number which appears on the certificate completed for this type (see paragraph 5.2. and Annex 2B) preceded by two figures indicating the sequence of the latest series of amendments to this Regulation.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and indelible.
In case of a Class 0 component, the working pressure shall also be marked in the vicinity of the approval mark mentioned in paragraph 5.4.
The specific equipment of vehicles using LPG in their propulsion system shall function in a correct and safe way.
The materials of the equipment which are in contact with LPG shall be compatible with it.

Those parts of equipment whose correct and safe functioning is liable to be influenced by LPG, high pressure or vibrations shall be submitted to relevant test procedures described in the annexes to this Regulation.
The provisions of paragraphs 6.2. to 6.13. shall be fulfilled.

The installation of LPG equipment approved by this Regulation shall comply with relevant electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements according to Regulation No. 10, 02 series of amendments, or equivalent.
The LPG containers shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 10 to this Regulation.
The container shall be equipped with the accessories listed in paragraphs 6.3.1.1. to 6.3.1.4., which may be either separate or combined (multivalve(s)).
The container shall be equipped with an 80 per cent stop valve.
The container shall be equipped with a pressure relief valve (discharge valve).
The container shall be equipped with a remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve.
The container shall be equipped with a pressure relief device (PRD).

The PRD shall be a fusible plug (temperature triggered) (fuse), or a pressure relief valve provided that it complies to paragraph 6.17.8.3., or a combination of the two, or any other equivalent technical solution provided that it ensures the same degree of performance.
The accessories mentioned in paragraphs 6.3.1., 6.3.2., 6.3.3. and 6.3.6. shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 3 to this Regulation.
The accessories mentioned in paragraph 6.3.5. shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 7 to this Regulation.
The other components, which are shown in Table 1, shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in the annexes which can be determined from the table.
The vaporizer and pressure regulator shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 6.
Shut-off valves, non-return valves, gas-tube pressure relief valves and service couplings shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 7.
Flexible hoses shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 8.
The filling unit shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 9.
Gas injection devices/gas mixing piece or injectors shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 11.
Gas dosage units shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 12.
Pressure sensors and temperature sensors shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 13.
The electronic control unit shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 14.
LPG filter units shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 5.
The pressure relief device shall be type approved pursuant to the provisions laid down in Annex 3.
A multi-component shall be type approved pursuant to the annexes applicable to the single components.
The connection between the float and the closing unit of the 80 per cent stop valve shall not be deformed under normal conditions of use.
If the 80 per cent stop valve of the container comprises a float, the float shall withstand an outside pressure of 4,500 kPa.

The closing unit of the device that limits the filling at 80 per cent +0/-5 per cent of the capacity of the container, for which the 80 per cent stop valve is designed, shall withstand a pressure of 6,750 kPa.
At the cut-off position of the 80 per cent stop valve, the filling rate at a differential pressure of 700 kPa shall not exceed 500 cm³/minute.
When the 80 per cent stop valve does not comprise any float, it shall not be possible to continue filling, after closing-off, at a rate exceeding 500 cm³/minute.
The 80 per cent stop valve device shall bear a permanent marking, indicating the container-type for which it has been designed, diameter and angle, and if applicable mounting indication.

Electrical operated devices containing LPG shall, in order to prevent in case of fracture of the component electric sparks on the surface of fracture, be insulated in a manner that no current is lead through LPG containing parts.

Electrical operated devices containing LPG shall, in order to prevent in case of fracture of the component electric sparks on the surface of fracture, have the electrical system of the device isolated from the body.

The electrical connections inside the boot and passengers compartment shall comply with at least the minimum protection degree class IP 40 according to IEC Standard 60529-1989+A1:1999+A2:2013 or IP40 according to ISO20653:2013.
All other electrical connections shall comply with at least the minimum protection degree class IP 54 according to IEC Standard.
The power supply bushing (fuel pump/actuators/fuel level sensor) to establish an isolated and tight electrical connection shall be of a hermetic sealed type.

In the case of valves activated by an electric/external power (e.g. 80 per cent stop valve, service valve, shut-off valves, non-return valves, gas tube pressure relief valve, service coupling), those valves shall be in "closed" position when their power is switched off.

Without prejudice to paragraph 1.7. of Annex 7 (commanded stop phases), a remotely controlled shut-off valve, when intended to be fitted as a component of an interconnected LPG-system for the purpose of paragraph 17.13.2.2., shall be submitted during approval to an endurance test according to paragraph 9. of Annex 16 with a number of cycles equal to 20,000.

The remotely controlled shut-off valve intended as a component of an interconnected LPG-system shall bear a clearly legible and indelible marking with the wording "ICS" and the approval mark according to paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation.

The materials constituting a device which are in contact with the heat exchange medium of a device when operating shall be compatible with that fluid and shall be designed to withstand a pressure of 200 kPa of the heat exchange medium.
The materials in contact with the heat exchange medium shall meet the prescriptions laid down in Annex 15, paragraph 17.
The compartment containing the heat exchange medium of the vaporizer/pressure regulator shall be leak proof at a pressure of 200 kPa.

A component consisting of both high pressure and low pressure parts shall be so designed to prevent a pressure build up in the low pressure part above 2.25 times the maximum working pressure for which it has been tested.
Components connected directly to the tank pressure shall be designed for the classification pressure of 3,000 kPa.
A component consisting of both high pressure and low pressure parts shall not vent to the motor compartment or outside of the vehicle.
The pressure regulator/vaporizer shall be so designed as to prevent any gas flow when the regulator/vaporizer unit is supplied with LPG at a pressure ≤ 4,500 kPa when the regulator is not operating.
Gas-tube pressure relief valves of Class 1 shall be so designed as to open at a pressure of 3,200 ± 100 kPa.
Gas-tube pressure relief valves of Class 1 shall not have internal leakage up to 3,000 kPa.
The pressure relief valve shall be mounted inside the container or on the container, in the area where the fuel is in gaseous state.
The pressure relief valve shall be so designed as to open at a pressure of 2,700 ± 100 kPa.

The flow capacity of the pressure relief valve, determined with compressed air at a pressure which is 20 per cent higher than the normal operating-pressure, shall be at least Q ≥ 10.66 ∙ A^0.82, in which Q = flow of air in standard m³/min (100 kPa absolute and temperature of 15 °C) and A = exterior surface of the container in m².
When the pressure relief valve is considered as a pressure relief device, the flow shall be at least 17.7 standard m³/min.
The pressure relief valve shall not have internal leakage up to 2,600 kPa.
The pressure relief device (fuse) shall be designed to open at a temperature of 120 ± 10 °C.

The pressure relief device (fuse) shall be designed to have, when opened, a flow capacity of Q ≥ 2.73 ∙ A, in which Q = flow of air in standard m3/min (100 kPa absolute and temperature of 15 °C) and A = exterior surface of the container in m².
The pressure relief device shall be mounted on the container in the gaseous zone.
The pressure relief device shall be fitted to the container in such a manner that it can discharge into the gas tight housing, when the presence of the gas tight housing is prescribed.
The pressure relief device (fuse) shall be tested according to the provisions described in Annex 3, paragraph 7.
The filling unit shall be equipped with at least one soft-seated non-return valve.
The filling unit shall not be dismountable by design.
The filling unit shall be protected against contamination.
The design and dimensions of the connecting area of the filling unit shall comply with those in the figures in Annex 9.
The outside filling unit shall be connected to the container by a hose or pipe.
For the K15 filling unit (Annex 9 – Figure 3), the dead volume between the front sealing surface and the front of the non-return valve shall not exceed 0.1 cm³.
For the K15 filling unit (Annex 9 – Figure 3), the flow through the connector at a pressure difference of 30 kPa shall be at least 60 litres/min, if tested with water.
For vehicles of category M1, the filling unit shall not be located below the body of the vehicle.
For vehicles of category M1, the filling unit shall respect the height provisions of paragraph 17.4.5.
The device to verify the level of liquid in the container shall be of an indirect type (for example magnetic) between the inside and outside of the container.
If the device to verify the level of liquid in the container is of a direct type, the electric power connections shall meet IP54 specifications according to IEC EN 60529:1997-06.
If the level indicator of the container comprises a float, the float shall withstand an outside pressure of 3,000 kPa.
The gas-tight housing outlet shall have a total free cross-section of at least 450 mm².
The gas-tight housing shall be leak-proof at a pressure of 10 kPa with the aperture(s) closed off, with a maximum allowed leak rate of 100 cm³/h vapour, and show no permanent deformation.
The gas-tight housing shall be designed to withstand a pressure of 50 kPa.
Service valves of Class 1 shall withstand a pressure of 6,750 kPa in the open and closed position.
The service valve shall not, at the shut-off position, allow an internal leak rate in the flow direction; there may be leak in the back flow direction.
The excess flow valve shall be mounted inside the container.
The excess flow valve shall be designed with a bypass to allow for equalization of pressures.
The excess flow valve shall cut off at a pressure difference over the valve of 90 kPa, and at this pressure difference the flow shall not exceed 8,000 cm³/min.
When the excess flow valve is at cut-off position, the flow through the by-pass shall not exceed 500 cm³/min. at a differential pressure of 700 kPa.

When a non-return valve is intended to be fitted as a component of an interconnected LPG-system for the purpose of paragraph 17.13.1.1., 17.13.1.2. or 17.13.2.1., it shall be submitted, during approval, to an endurance test according to paragraph 9.7. of Annex 16.

When a non-return valve is intended to be fitted as a component of an interconnected LPG-system for the purpose of paragraph 17.13.1.1., 17.13.1.2. or 17.13.2.1., the valve shall bear a clearly legible and indelible marking with the wording "ICS" and the approval mark according to paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation.

When intended to be fitted as components or parts of an interconnected LPG-system, non-metallic, metallic or a mixture of metallic and non-metallic LPG components, including flexible hoses and their elements, and non-metallic, metallic or a mixture of metallic and non-metallic parts of LPG components which may come into contact with petrol shall meet the requirements specified in Annex 19 to this Regulation.
Non-metallic, metallic or a mixture of metallic and non-metallic components or components containing non-metallic parts shall bear an approval mark according to Annex A, Appendix 1.
The LPG equipment as installed in the vehicle shall function in such a manner that the working pressure for which it has been designed and approved cannot be exceeded.
All parts of the LPG system shall be type approved for individual parts pursuant to Part I of this Regulation.
The materials used in the LPG system shall be suitable for use with LPG.
All parts of the LPG system shall be fastened in a proper way.
The LPG system shall show no leaks.

The LPG system shall be installed such that it has the best possible protection against damage, such as damage due to moving vehicle components, collision, grit or due to the loading or unloading of the vehicle or the shifting of those loads.

Notwithstanding paragraph 17.1.6., when the LPG-container and its accessories are located outside the vehicle, it shall be possible to make an external inspection (e.g. for periodic technical inspection) of them, according to the specifications of the manufacturer, without the use of tools to dismantle, but with visual aids, e.g. lamps, mirrors or endoscopes.
No appliances shall be connected to the LPG system other than those strictly required for the proper operation of the engine of the motor vehicle.

No component of the LPG system, including any protective materials which form part of such components, shall project beyond the external surface of the vehicle, with the exception of the filling unit if this does not project more than 10 mm beyond the nominal line of the body panel.

With the exception of the LPG fuel container, in no cross section of the vehicle shall any component of the LPG system, including any protective material which forms part of such components, extend beyond the lower edge of the vehicle unless another part of the vehicle, within a radius of 150 mm is situated lower.
No component of the LPG system shall be located within 100 mm of the exhaust or similar heat source, unless such components are adequately shielded against heat.
An LPG system shall contain at least the following components, as listed in paragraphs 17.3.1.1. to 17.3.1.13.
The LPG system shall contain at least an 80 per cent stop valve.
The LPG system shall contain at least a pressure relief valve.
The LPG system shall contain at least a remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve.
The LPG system shall contain at least a pressure regulator and vaporizer, which may be combined (these components might not be necessary in case of liquid LPG injection).
The LPG system shall contain at least a remotely controlled shut-off valve.
The LPG system shall contain at least gas tubes and hoses.
The LPG system shall contain at least gas-carrying connections between the LPG system components.
The LPG system shall contain at least an injector or gas injection device or gas mixing piece.
The LPG system shall contain at least an electronic control unit.
The LPG system shall contain at least a pressure relief device (fuse).
The fuel container shall be permanently installed in the vehicle.
The fuel container shall not be installed in the engine compartment.
The fuel container shall be installed in the correct position, according to the instructions from the container manufacturer.
The fuel container shall be installed such that there is no metal to metal contact, other than at the permanent fixing points of the container.
The fuel container shall have permanent fixing points to secure it to the motor vehicle or the container shall be secured to the motor vehicle by a container frame and container straps.
When the vehicle is ready for use the fuel container shall not be less than 200 mm above the road surface.
The fuel container(s) shall be mounted and fixed so that the accelerations specified for the vehicle category can be absorbed (without damage occurring) when the containers are full.

For vehicles of categories M1 and N1, the fuel container(s) shall be mounted and fixed so that an acceleration of 20 g in the direction of travel can be absorbed (without damage occurring) when the containers are full.

For vehicles of categories M1 and N1, the fuel container(s) shall be mounted and fixed so that an acceleration of 8 g horizontally perpendicular to the direction of travel can be absorbed (without damage occurring) when the containers are full.
The remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve shall be installed directly on the fuel container, without any intervening fittings.

The remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve shall be controlled such that it is automatically closed when the engine is not running, irrespective of the position of the ignition switch, and shall remain closed as long as the engine is not running.
If the remotely controlled service valve is closed during commanded stop phases, the valve shall comply with paragraph 4.7. of Annex 3.
The spring-loaded pressure relief valve shall be installed in the fuel container in such a manner that it is connected to the vapour space and can discharge to the surrounding atmosphere.

The automatic filling level limiter shall be suitable for the fuel container it is fitted to and shall be installed in the appropriate position to ensure that the container cannot be filled to more than 80 per cent.
The level indicator shall be suitable for the fuel container it is fitted to and shall be installed in the appropriate position.

A gas-tight housing over the container fittings, which fulfils the requirements of paragraphs 17.6.5.2. to 17.6.5.5., shall be fitted to the fuel container, unless the container is installed outside the vehicle and the container fittings are protected against dirt and water.
The gas-tight housing shall be in open connection with the atmosphere, where necessary through a connecting hose and a lead-through.
The ventilation opening of the gas-tight housing shall point downwards at the point of exit from the motor vehicle.
The ventilation opening of the gas-tight housing shall not discharge into a wheel arch, nor shall it be aimed at a heat source such as the exhaust.
Any connecting hose and lead-through in the bottom of the bodywork of the motor vehicle for ventilation of the gas-tight housing shall have a minimum clear opening of 450 mm².
If a gas tube, other tube or any electrical wiring is installed in the connecting hose and lead-through for ventilation of the gas-tight housing, the clear opening shall also be at least 450 mm².
The gas-tight housing and connecting hoses shall be gas-tight at a pressure of 10 kPa with the apertures closed off, and show no permanent deformation, with a maximum allowed leak rate of 100 cm³/h.
The connecting hose shall be secured in a proper way to the gas-tight housing and the lead-through to ensure that a gas-tight joint is formed.
Gas tubes shall be of seamless type made of either copper or stainless steel or steel with corrosion-resistant coating.
If seamless copper is used the gas tube shall be protected by a rubber or plastic sleeve.
The outer diameter of Class 1 gas tubes made of copper shall not exceed 12 mm with a wall thickness of at least 0.8 mm.
Gas tubes of Class 1 from steel and stainless steel shall not exceed 25 mm outer diameter with, for gas services, an appropriate wall thickness.
Gas tubes of non-seamless type shall comply with the applicable tests according to the provisions of Annex 15.
Gas pipes made of a non-metallic material shall comply with the requirements of this Regulation, paragraph 6.7.
Where a gas tube is replaced by a gas hose, the hose shall fulfil the requirements of this Regulation, paragraph 6.7.
Gas tubes, other than non-metallic gas tubes, shall be secured such that they shall not be subjected to vibration or stresses.
Gas hoses and non-metallic gas tubes shall be secured such that they shall not be subjected to stresses.
At the fixing point the gas tube or hose shall be fitted with a protective material.
Gas tubes or hoses shall not be located at jacking points.
At passages the gas tubes or hoses, whether or not fitted with a protective sleeve, shall be fitted with protective material.

Soldered or welded joints and bite-type compression joints shall not be used, except that soldering or welding can be permitted for connecting the individual parts of detachable couplings to the gas tube or component.
Gas tubes shall only be connected by fittings that are compatible with regard to corrosion.
Stainless steel tubes shall only be joined by stainless steel fittings.
Distributing-blocks shall be made of corrosion-resistant material.
Gas tubes shall be connected by appropriate joints, for example, two-part compression joints in steel tubes and joints with olives tapered on both sides or two flanges in copper tubes.
Gas tubes shall be connected with appropriate connections.
Under no circumstances shall couplings be used whereby the gas tube will be damaged.
The burst pressure of the mounted couplings shall be the same or higher as specified for the tube.
The number of joints in the LPG system shall be limited to a minimum.
Any joints shall be made in locations where access is possible for inspection.

In a passenger compartment or enclosed luggage compartment the gas tube or hose shall be no longer than reasonably required; this provision is fulfilled when the gas tube or hose does not extend further than from the fuel container to the side of vehicle.

There shall be no gas-conveying connections in the passenger compartment or enclosed luggage compartment with the exception of (a) the connections on the gas-tight housing; and (b) the connection between the gas tube or hose and the filling unit if this connection is fitted with a sleeve which is resistant against LPG and any leaking gas will be discharged directly into the atmosphere.
A remotely controlled shut-off valve shall be installed in the gas tube from the LPG container to the pressure regulator/vaporizer, as close as possible to the pressure regulator/vaporizer.

The remotely controlled shut-off valve shall be installed such that the fuel supply is cut off when the engine is not running or, if the vehicle is also equipped with another fuel system, when the other fuel is selected.
If the remotely controlled shut-off valve is closed during commanded stop phases, the valve shall comply with paragraph 1.7. of Annex 7.
The filling unit shall be secured against rotation.
The filling unit shall be protected against dirt and water.
When the LPG container is installed in the passenger compartment or an enclosed (luggage) compartment, the filling unit shall be located at the outside of the vehicle.
The electrical components of the LPG system shall be protected against overloads.
At least one separate fuse shall be provided in the supply cable of the electrical components of the LPG system.
The fuse shall be installed in a known location where it can be reached without the use of tools.
The electrical power to LPG system components which also carry gas shall not be conducted by a gas tube.
All electrical components installed in a part of the LPG system where the pressure exceeds 20 kPa shall be connected and insulated in a manner that no current is led through LPG containing parts.
Electrical cables shall be adequately protected against damage.
The electrical connections inside the boot and passengers compartment shall comply with protection degree class IP 40 according to IEC Standard 60529-1989+A1:1999.
All electrical connections other than those inside the boot and passengers compartment shall comply with protection degree class IP 54 according to IEC Standard 60529-1989+A1:1999.
Vehicles with more than one fuel system shall have a fuel selection system.
The electrical connections and components in the gas-tight housing shall be constructed such that no sparks are generated.

The pressure relief device shall be fitted to the fuel container(s) in such a manner that it can discharge into the gas tight housing, when its presence is prescribed, if that gas tight housing fulfils the requirements of paragraph 17.6.5.

In an LPG-petrol bi-fuel vehicle, means shall be provided to prevent any flow of LPG into the petrol tank; two non-return valves along the flow line complying with paragraph 6.17.14.1. are considered as meeting this requirement.

In order to prevent flows of petrol into the LPG container occurring during switch-over operations from leading to an overfilling of the LPG tank (i.e. above 80 per cent of its capacity which means 80 per cent liquid and 20 per cent gaseous fuel), the LPG-system shall contain an Electronic Control Unit complying also with paragraph 6. of Annex 14.
A remotely controlled shut-off valve complying with the provisions of paragraph 6.17.3.3. shall be installed along the flow line.
Means shall be provided to prevent that flows of petrol into the LPG fuel container could lead to a content of petrol higher than 16 per cent of the actual volume contained in the LPG tank.
The measure preventing petrol content higher than 16 per cent of the actual volume contained in the LPG tank shall be demonstrated in accordance with the procedures laid down in Annex 20.

The requirement that petrol content in the LPG tank not exceed 16 per cent of the actual volume shall be fulfilled also in case of faults by use of a malfunction indication to the driver, and optionally activation of limp home mode.

Non-metallic, metallic or a mixture of metallic and non-metallic LPG components, including flexible hoses and their elements, and non-metallic, metallic or a mixture of metallic and non-metallic parts of LPG components which may come into contact with petrol shall comply with the requirements set out in paragraph 6.18.
The ECU complying with the requirements of paragraph 17.13.2.2. shall be installed in vehicles where the flushed volume is less than or equal to 0.4 litre.
The ECU complying with the requirements of paragraph 17.13.2.2. shall be installed in vehicles equipped with a LPG container having a capacity higher than 20 litres.

The indication mark of technical modification (A in the example), preceded by the star symbol, shall be on the approval mark only of the accessories of the container (multivalve or, when approved separately, pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and pressure relief device).

The approval mark of non-metallic, metallic or mixed LPG components compatible with petrol shall be affixed to the LPG component or to an identification plate placed in the engine compartment on a visible fixed irreplaceable chassis part, when the component is to be installed in such a way that it will no longer be readily accessible.
The approval mark affixed to a vehicle approved with regard to the installation of specific equipment for the use of LPG for propulsion shall be arranged according to Model A or Model B of Annex 2C.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall be classified as Class 3 (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of the 80 per cent stop valve shall be 3,000 kPa.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 65 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special tests conditions are applicable.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.1. regarding the 80 per cent stop valve.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.2. regarding the electrical insulation.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.3.1. on valves activated by electrical power.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the overpressure test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 4.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the external leakage test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 5.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the high temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 6.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the low temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 7.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the seat leakage test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 8.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the endurance test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 9.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the operational tests in accordance with Annex 16, para. 10.
For non-metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the LPG compatibility test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 11.
For metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the corrosion resistance test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 12.
For non-metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the resistance to dry heat test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 13.
For non-metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the ozone ageing test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 14.
For non-metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the creep test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 15.
For non-metallic parts, the 80 per cent stop valve shall pass the temperature cycle test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 16.
The level indicator shall be classified as Class 1 (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of the level indicator shall be 3,000 kPa.
The level indicator shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 65 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special tests conditions are applicable.
The level indicator shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.11. regarding the level indicator.
The level indicator shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.2. regarding the electrical insulation.
The level indicator shall pass the overpressure test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 4.
The level indicator shall pass the external leakage test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 5.
The level indicator shall pass the high temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 6.
The level indicator shall pass the low temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 7.
For non-metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the LPG compatibility test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 11.
For metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the corrosion resistance test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 12.
For non-metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the resistance to dry heat test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 13.
For non-metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the ozone ageing test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 14.
For non-metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the creep test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 15.
For non-metallic parts, the level indicator shall pass the temperature cycle test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 16.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and components connecting it with the gaseous phase inside the LPG container shall be classified as Class 3 (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of the pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and components connecting it with the gaseous phase inside the LPG container shall be 3,000 kPa.

The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and components connecting it with the gaseous phase inside the LPG container shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 65 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special tests conditions are applicable.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.17.8. regarding the pressure relief valve (discharge valve).
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the overpressure test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 4.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the external leakage test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 5.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the high temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 6.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the low temperature test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 7.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the seat leakage test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 8.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the endurance test (with 200 operation cycles) in accordance with Annex 16, para. 9.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the operational test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 10.
For non-metallic parts, the pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the LPG compatibility test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 11.
For metallic parts, the pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the corrosion resistance test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 12.
For non-metallic parts, the pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and connecting components shall pass the resistance to dry heat test in accordance with Annex 16, para. 13.
