For containers with circumferential welds only (two sections), on test-pieces taken from the places shown in Figures 2a and 2b of Appendix 2 to this annex, the tests specified in paragraph 2.1.2.1.1. shall be carried out, with the exception of (c), (e) and (f) which are not applicable.
The values determined for yield stress, tensile strength and elongation after break shall comply with the characteristics of the metal as required in paragraph 1.3. of this annex.
The tensile strength value obtained in the tensile test on welds shall meet the minimum levels required by EN 10120.

Cracks shall not appear in the test-piece when it is bent round a mandrel as long as the inside edges are separated by a distance not greater than the diameter of the mandrel +3a (see Figure 1 of Appendix 3 to this annex).
Containers subjected to the burst test under hydraulic pressure shall bear the inscriptions which it is proposed to affix on the section of the container subjected to pressure.
The measured bursting pressure (Pr) of the container shall not under any circumstances be less than 2.25 ∙ 3,000 = 6,750 kPa.
The specific change in the volume of the metal container at the time of bursting shall not be less than 20 per cent if the length of the metal container is greater than the diameter.
The specific change in the volume of the metal container at the time of bursting shall not be less than 17 per cent if the length of the metal container is equal to or less than the diameter.
The burst test shall not cause any fragmentation of the container.

The main fracture shall not show any brittleness, i.e. the edges of the fracture shall not be radial but shall be at an angle to a diametrical plane and display a reduction of area throughout their thickness.
For metal containers the fracture shall not reveal an inherent defect in the metal.
For metal containers the weld shall be at least as strong as the original metal but preferably stronger.

The containers representative of the type of container submitted for approval (without accessories but with the outlets closed off) shall withstand an inner hydraulic pressure of 3,000 kPa without leakages or becoming permanently distorted, according to the requirements of paragraphs 2.3.2. to 2.3.5.
After the hydraulic test the container shall show no signs of permanent deformation.
Welds shall not have the following defects: cracks, inadequate welds or inadequate penetration of the weld.
For the container wall thickness ≥ 4 mm, any gas inclusion measuring not more than a/4 mm is regarded as acceptable.

For the container wall thickness ≥ 4 mm, any gas inclusion measuring more than a/4 mm but not more than a/3 mm, which is more than 25 mm away from other gas inclusion measuring more than a/4 mm and measuring not more than a/3 mm, is regarded as acceptable.

For the container wall thickness ≥ 4 mm, any elongated inclusion or any group of rounded inclusions in a row where the length represented (over a weld length of 12a) is not greater than 6 mm is regarded as acceptable.
For the container wall thickness ≥ 4 mm, gas inclusions over any 100 mm weld length, where the total area of all the figures is not greater than 2a mm², are regarded as acceptable.
For the container wall thickness < 4 mm, any gas inclusion measuring not more than a/2 mm is regarded as acceptable.

For the container wall thickness < 4 mm, any gas inclusion measuring more than a/2 mm but not more than a/1.5 mm, which is more than 25 mm away from other gas inclusion measuring more than a/2 mm and measuring not more than a/1.5 mm, is regarded as acceptable.
The macroscopic examination of a full transverse section of the weld shall show a complete fusion on the surface treated with any acid from the macro-preparation.
The macroscopic examination of a full transverse section of the weld shall not show any assembly fault or a significant inclusion or other defects.
The fusion of the welded metal with the parent metal shall be smooth and free from etching.
There shall be no cracks, notching or porous patches in the welded surface and the surface adjacent to the wall.
The welded surface shall be regular and even.
Where a butt weld has been used, the excess thickness shall not exceed 1/4 of the width of the weld.

A multivalve or, when approved separately, pressure relief valve (discharge valve) and pressure relief device, extended for technical modifications and marked in accordance to Annex 2A, shall have a new bonfire test.
In the bonfire test, any failure during the test of a valve, fitting or tubing that is not part of the intended protection system for the design shall invalidate the result.
In the bonfire test, a burst of the container shall invalidate the test result.
In the bonfire test, a pressure of more than 3,700 kPa, i.e. 136 per cent of the set pressure of the PRV (2,700 kPa), during the test shall invalidate the test result.
In the bonfire test, a pressure between 3,000 and 3,700 kPa shall only invalidate the test result in case visible plastic deformation is observed.

In the bonfire test, in case the behaviour of the protection system does not comply with the specification of the manufacturer and it leads to a mitigating test condition the result shall be invalidated.
In the case where a container can be installed in more than one position in the vehicle, each position shall be impact tested.
After the impact test, the container shall be submitted to an external leak test as defined in paragraph 2.3.6.3. of this annex.
After the impact test, the container shall comply with the external leak test requirements as defined in paragraph 2.3.6.3. of this annex.
One finished container shall be drop tested at ambient temperature without internal pressurization or attached valves.
The same empty container shall be dropped in a horizontal position.
The same empty container shall be dropped vertically on each end.
The same empty container shall be dropped at an angle of 45°.
Following the drop test, the containers shall be submitted to an ambient temperature pressure cycling test according the requirements of paragraph 2.3.6.1. of this annex.
After the drop test, the containers shall comply with the requirements of the ambient temperature pressure cycling test according the requirements of paragraph 2.3.6.1. of this annex.

A torque of 2 times the valve or PRD installation torque specified by the manufacturer shall be applied to each end boss of the container, first in the direction to tighten a threaded connection, then in the untightening direction, and finally again in the tightening direction.
After the torque is applied, the container shall be subjected to an external leak test in accordance with the requirements shown in paragraph 2.3.6.3 of this annex.
After the boss torque test, the container shall comply with the requirements of the external leak test as shown in paragraph 2.3.6.3. of this annex.
A finished container shall be exposed for 100 hours to a 30 per cent sulphuric acid solution (battery acid with specific gravity of 1.219) while pressurized to 3,000 kPa.
After the acid exposure, the container shall be submitted to a burst test as defined in paragraph 2.2. of this annex.
After the acid environment test, the burst pressure measured shall be at least 85 per cent of the container burst pressure.

If the outer layer has a mechanical (load carrying) function, the container shall be burst tested according to the requirements of paragraph 2.2. of this annex, after exposing to a representative UV-radiation.
When the outer layer has a mechanical function, the container shall comply with the burst test requirements as defined in paragraph 2.2. of this annex after the UV test.
The part of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece with a maximum regulated pressure during operation of 450 kPa shall be of Class 2 (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The part of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece with a maximum regulated pressure during operation of 120 kPa shall be of Class 2A (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2 of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be 450 kPa.
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2A of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be 120 kPa.

When the fuel pump is mounted outside the container, the gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 120 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special test conditions are applicable.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall meet paragraph 6.17.2., Provisions regarding the electrical insulation.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall meet paragraph 6.17.2.1., Provisions regarding the insulation class.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall meet paragraph 6.17.3.1., Provisions when the power is switched off.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall meet paragraph 6.17.4.1., Heat exchange medium (compatibility and pressure requirements).
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the overpressure test according to Annex 16, para. 4.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the external leakage test according to Annex 16, para. 5.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the high temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 6.
The gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the low temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 7.
The non-metallic parts of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test according to Annex 16, para. 11.
The metallic parts of the gas injection device or gas mixing piece shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test according to Annex 16, para. 12.
The fuel rail shall be of Class 0, 1, 2 or 2A (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2 of the fuel rail shall be 450 kPa.
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2A of the fuel rail shall be 120 kPa.
The fuel rail shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 120 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special test conditions are applicable.
The fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the overpressure test according to Annex 16, para. 4.
The fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the external leakage test according to Annex 16, para. 5.
The fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the high temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 6.
The fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the low temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 7.
The non-metallic parts of the fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test according to Annex 16, para. 11.
The metallic parts of the fuel rail of Class 2 and/or 2A shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test according to Annex 16, para. 12.
The part of the gas dosage unit with a maximum regulated pressure during operation of 450 kPa shall be of Class 2 (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The part of the gas dosage unit with a maximum regulated pressure during operation of 120 kPa shall be of Class 2A (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2 of the gas dosage unit shall be 450 kPa.
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2A of the gas dosage unit shall be 120 kPa.
The gas dosage unit shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 120 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special test conditions are applicable.
The gas dosage unit shall meet paragraph 6.17.2., Provisions regarding the electrical insulation.
The gas dosage unit shall meet paragraph 6.17.3.1., Provisions on valves activated by electrical power.
The gas dosage unit shall meet paragraph 6.17.4., Heat exchange medium (compatibility and pressure requirements).
The gas dosage unit shall meet paragraph 6.17.5., Overpressure bypass security.
The parts of the gas dosage unit (Class 2 or 2A) shall be leakproof with the outlet(s) of that part closed.
The gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the overpressure test according to Annex 16, para. 4.
The gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the external leakage test according to Annex 16, para. 5.
The gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the high temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 6.
The gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the low temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 7.
The non-metallic parts of the gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test according to Annex 16, para. 11.
The metallic parts of the gas dosage unit shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test according to Annex 16, para. 12.
Pressure and temperature sensors shall be of Class 0, 1, 2 or 2A (according to Figure 1, para. 2.).
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2 of a pressure or temperature sensor shall be 450 kPa.
The classification pressure of parts of Class 2A of a pressure or temperature sensor shall be 120 kPa.
The pressure and temperature sensor shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 120 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special test conditions are applicable.
The pressure and temperature sensor shall meet paragraph 6.17.2., Provisions regarding the electrical insulation.
The pressure and temperature sensor shall meet paragraph 6.17.4.1., Heat exchange medium (compatibility and pressure requirements).
The pressure and temperature sensor shall meet paragraph 6.17.6.2., Gas flow prevention.
The pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the overpressure test according to Annex 16, para. 4.
The pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the external leakage test according to Annex 16, para. 5.
The pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the high temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 6.
The pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the low temperature test according to Annex 16, para. 7.
The non-metallic parts of the pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test according to Annex 16, para. 11.
The metallic parts of the pressure and temperature sensor of Class 2 or 2A shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test according to Annex 16, para. 12.

The electronic control unit shall establish the cut-off of the remotely-controlled service valve(s), cut-off valves and fuel pump of the LPG system in case of a broken fuel supply pipe or/and in case of stalling of the engine.
The switching off delay of the service cut-off valves after stalling of the engine shall not be more than 5 seconds.
The electronic control unit shall comply with relevant electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements according to Regulation No. 10, 02 series of amendments or equivalent.
Electrical failure of the vehicle system shall not lead to uncontrolled opening of any valve.
The output of the electronic control unit shall be inactive when the electric power is switched off or removed.

When the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) is intended to be fitted as a component of an interconnected LPG-system, it shall inhibit, by controlling the fuel selection system, the vehicle operation in petrol mode after each switch-over operation to LPG mode until a volume of liquid fuel equivalent to that flown into the LPG tank during such an operation is consumed.

When the ECU is fitted as a component of an interconnected LPG-system and permits the switch over to petrol mode because of a fault in the LPG-system, such a fault shall be clearly indicated to the driver.

In case of the inoperability of the interconnected LPG-system, a remotely controlled shut-off valve complying with the requirements of paragraph 6.17.3.3. shall be installed along the flow line in order to prevent any flow of petrol into the LPG container after switching-over to petrol mode.
The maximum volume of liquid fuel that flows during a switch-over operation shall not exceed 0.4 litre.
The minimum volume of the tank shall not be lower than 20 litres.
In the test of paragraph 6.2., petrol mode shall be disabled until a volume of liquid fuel equal to 0.4 litre is consumed.
The ECU shall bear a clearly legible and indelible marking with the wording "ICS".
The ECU shall bear a clearly legible and indelible marking with the value of 0.4 litre.
The ECU shall bear a clearly legible and indelible marking with the approval mark according to paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation.
The classification pressure of gas tube(s) and couplings of Class 1 shall be 3,000 kPa.
The classification pressure of gas tube(s) and couplings of Class 2 shall be 450 kPa.
The gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be designed for temperatures of -20 °C to 120 °C; for temperatures exceeding these values, special test conditions are applicable.
The couplings shall be compatible with the gas tube.
Specific care shall be taken against galvanic corrosion in the gas tube and its couplings.
Only straight longitudinal welding (in the direction of the tube itself) shall be used in gas tubes of non-seamless type.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the overpressure test of Annex 16, para. 4.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the external leakage test of Annex 16, para. 5.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the high temperature test of Annex 16, para. 6.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the low temperature test of Annex 16, para. 7.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, non-metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test of Annex 16, para. 11.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test of Annex 16, para. 12.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, non-metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the resistance to dry heat test of Annex 16, para. 13.
For parts of Classes 0 and 1, non-metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the ozone ageing test of Annex 16, para. 14.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the overpressure test of Annex 16, para. 4.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the external leakage test of Annex 16, para. 5.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the high temperature test of Annex 16, para. 6.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the low temperature test of Annex 16, para. 7.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, non-metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test of Annex 16, para. 11.
For parts of Class 2 or 2A, metallic parts of the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test of Annex 16, para. 12.
The gas tube and its coupling(s) shall be tested for an endurance test consisting of 100,000 cycles, one cycle consisting of a pressure ramp from 15 per cent·WP up to WP.
After the endurance test, the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall comply with the leakage test of Annex 16, paragraphs 5., 6. and 7. and with the overpressure test according to Annex 16, paragraph 4.

After bending, the ends of the gas tube shall be closed and the gas tube shall be subjected to the overpressure test according to Annex 16, paragraph 4. and, at its completion, tested according to the leakage test of Annex 16, paragraphs 5., 6. and 7.

A coupling designed to be connected directly to threaded fittings shall be capable of withstanding, without deformation, breakage or leakage, a torque effort of 150 per cent of the rated installation value delivered by the manufacturer.
After the vibration test the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall comply with the leakage test of Annex 16, paragraphs 5., 6. and 7. and with the overpressure test according to Annex 16, paragraph 4.

The force (F), in Newton, required to pull apart the gas tube from its coupling(s) shall be that calculated as F = (π∙d²∙P)/10 where d is the internal diameter, in millimetres; P is the maximum working pressure, in bar.
All gas tubes and its couplings having brass components shall be subjected to the brass material compatibility test according to Annex 16, paragraph 12.2.

After the brass material compatibility test the gas tube and its coupling(s) shall comply with the leakage test of Annex 16, paragraphs 5., 6. and 7. and with the overpressure test according to Annex 16, paragraph 4.
The tests determined by the classification of the components shall be performed for type approval of the components or parts of the components.
LPG components shall be subjected to the test procedures shown in Table 1 as applicable to their classification.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the overpressure test of paragraph 4.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the external leakage test of paragraph 5.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the high temperature test of paragraph 6.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the low temperature test of paragraph 7.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the seat leakage test of paragraph 8.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the endurance / functional tests of paragraph 9.
Components of Class 0 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the operational test of paragraph 10.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the LPG compatibility test of paragraph 11.
Components of Class 0, Class 1, Class 2(A) and Class 3 shall be subjected to the corrosion resistance test of paragraph 12.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the resistance to dry heat test of paragraph 13.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the ozone ageing test of paragraph 14.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the creep test of paragraph 15.
Components of Class 0, Class 1 and Class 3 shall be subjected to the temperature cycle test of paragraph 16.
Components of Class 0 and Class 2(A) shall be subjected to the compatibility with heat exchange fluid test of paragraph 17.

An LPG containing component shall withstand without any visible evidence of rupture or permanent distortion a hydraulic test pressure which is determined by Table 1 (of 2.25 times the maximum classification pressure) during minimal 1 minute with the outlet of the high pressure part plugged.
For a Class 0 component, the classification pressure is WP and the hydraulic test pressure for the over-pressure test shall be 2.25 WP.
For a Class 1 component, the classification pressure is 3,000 kPa and the hydraulic test pressure for the over-pressure test shall be 6,750 kPa.
For a Class 3 component, the classification pressure is 3,000 kPa or WP and the hydraulic test pressure for the over-pressure test shall be 6,750 kPa or 2.25 WP.
For a Class 2 component, the classification pressure is 450 kPa and the hydraulic test pressure for the over-pressure test shall be 1,015 kPa.

A component shall be free from leakage through stem or body seals or other joints, and shall not show evidence of porosity in casting when tested as described in paragraph 5.3. at any aerostatic pressure between 0 and the pressure shown in Table 3; these prescriptions are deemed to be satisfied if the provisions of paragraph 5.4. are met.
For a Class 0 component, the test pressure for the leakage test shall be 1.5 WP (classification pressure WP).
For a Class 1 component, the test pressure for the leakage test shall be 4,500 kPa (classification pressure 3,000 kPa).
For a Class 2 component, the test pressure for the leakage test shall be 675 kPa (classification pressure 450 kPa).
For a Class 3 component, the test pressure for the leakage test shall be 6,750 kPa (classification pressure 3,000 kPa).

The external leakage shall be lower than the requirements stated in the annexes or, if no requirements are mentioned, lower than 15 cm³/hour with the outlet plugged, when submitted to a gas pressure equal to the leakage test pressure.

An LPG containing component shall not leak more than 15 cm³/hour with the outlet plugged when submitted to a gas pressure at maximum operating temperature, as indicated in the annexes, equal to the leakage test pressure (Table 3, paragraph 5.3.).

An LPG containing component shall not leak more than 15 cm³/hour with the outlet plugged when submitted to a gas pressure, at the minimum operating temperature (-20 °C), equal to the leakage test pressure (Table 3, paragraph 5.3.).

The seat of a shut-off valve, when in the closed position, shall be free from leakage at any aerostatic pressure between 0 to 3,000 kPa or from 0 to WP in accordance with the classification pressure of the valve.
A non-return valve provided with a resilient seat, when in the closed position, shall not leak when subjected to any aerostatic pressure between 50 and 3,000 kPa.

A non-return valve provided with a metal-to-metal seat, when in the closed position, shall not leak at a rate exceeding 0.50 dm³/hour when subjected to an inlet pressure up to the test pressure according to Table 3 in paragraph 5.3.
The seat of the upper non-return valve used in the assembly of a filling unit, when in the closed position, shall be free from leakage at any aerostatic pressure between 50 and 3,000 kPa.
The gas-tube pressure relief valve shall not have internal leakage up to 3,000 kPa or up to WP, in accordance with the classification pressure of the valve.
The pressure relief valve (discharge valve) shall not have internal leakage up to 2,600 kPa.

A filling unit or service valve shall be capable of conforming to the applicable leakage test requirements of paragraphs 5. and 8. above, after being subjected to a number of cycles of opening and closing as mentioned in the annexes to this Regulation.
The 80 per cent stop valve shall be capable of withstanding 6,000 complete filling cycles to the maximum filling degree.
The pressure regulator and vaporizer shall be able to withstand 50,000 cycles without any failure when tested according to the procedure of sub-paragraphs (a) to (g) of paragraph 9.6.

Before being subjected to a flow capacity test, the start-to-discharge pressure of each of three samples of a pressure relief valve of a specific size, design, and setting shall be within +3 per cent of the average of the pressures.

Before being subjected to a flow capacity test, the start-to-discharge pressure of any one of the three pressure relief valves shall be not less than 95 per cent, not more than 105 per cent, of the set pressure marked on the valve.
The resealing pressure of a pressure relief valve before being subjected to a flow capacity test shall be not less than 50 per cent of the initially observed start-to-discharge pressure.
The flow capacity of each of three samples of a pressure relief valve of a specific size, design, and setting shall fall within a range of 10 per cent of the highest observed capacity.
During flow capacity tests on each pressure relief valve, there shall be no evidence of chattering or other abnormal operating condition.
The blow-down pressure of each pressure relief valve shall be not less than 65 per cent of the initially recorded start-to-discharge pressure.
A flow capacity test on a pressure relief valve shall be conducted at a flow rating pressure of 120 per cent of the maximum set pressure.

Subsequent to flow capacity tests, the start-to-discharge pressure of a pressure relief valve shall be not less than 85 per cent of the initial start-to-discharge pressure recorded under test No. 1 of paragraph 10.1.2.

Subsequent to flow capacity tests, the resealing pressure of a pressure relief valve shall be not less than 80 per cent of the initial resealing pressure recorded under test No. 1 of paragraph 10.1.2.

An excess flow valve shall operate at not more than 10 per cent above, nor less than 20 per cent below the rated closing flow capacity specified by the manufacturer during the operation tests described below.
An excess flow valve shall close automatically at a pressure differential across the valve of not more than 100 kPa during the operation tests described below.
An excess flow valve used in the assembly of a filling unit shall close automatically at a pressure differential of not more than 138 kPa when tested as described below.

Testing of the good function of the device limiting the filling degree of the container shall be performed at filling speeds of 20, 50 and 80 l/min or at the maximum flow rate under an upstream pressure of 700 kPa abs.
The device limiting the filling degree of the container shall be capable of withstanding 6,000 complete filling cycles to the maximum filling degree.
Any device limiting the filling degree of the container and operating by a float shall limit the degree of filling of the container to 80 per cent or less of its capacity.
Any device limiting the filling degree of the container and operating by a float shall not allow, at the cut-off position, any filling of the container at a rate exceeding 0.5 litre/minute.

Any device limiting the filling degree of the container and operating by a float, after the tests verifying the filling limits, shall be subjected to one of the test procedures laid down in paragraph 10.5.5. or 10.5.6. to ensure that it withstands expected dynamic vibrational stresses and that performance degradations or malfunctions are not produced by the service vibration environment.
After having been subjected to one of the vibration test procedures described above, the device shall show no mechanical failures.

The device is deemed to conform to the vibration test requirements only if the filling degree at the cut-off position and the filling rate allowed at the cut-off position do not exceed the prescribed limits and do not exceed by more than 10 per cent the values preceding the vibration test procedure.
A synthetic part in contact with LPG-liquid shall not show excessive volume change or loss of weight.
Resistance of the synthetic part to LPG-liquid shall be tested to n-pentane according to ISO 1817 with medium n-pentane, temperature 23 °C (tolerance acc. to ISO 1817) and immersion period 72 hours.
The synthetic part in contact with LPG-liquid shall show a maximum change in volume of 20 per cent in the n-pentane test.
After storage in air at a temperature of 40 °C for a period of 48 hours, the mass of the synthetic part compared to the original value shall not decrease more than 5 per cent.

A metal LPG containing component shall comply with the leakage tests mentioned in 4, 5, 6 and 7 after having been submitted to a 144 hours salt spray test according to ISO 9227, with all connections closed, or alternatively to the optional test of paragraph 12.1.1.

As the optional test, a metal LPG containing component shall comply with the leakage tests mentioned in paragraphs 4, 5, 6 and 7 after having been submitted to a salt spray test according to IEC 68-2-52 Kb: Salt Spray Fog Test.

A copper or brass LPG containing component shall comply with the leakage tests mentioned in paragraphs 4, 5, 6 and 7 after having been submitted to 24 hours immersion in Ammonia according to ISO 6957 with all connections closed.
The dry heat resistance test shall be done in compliance with ISO 188, with the test piece exposed to air at a temperature equal to the maximum operating temperature for 168 hours.
After the dry heat exposure, the change in tensile strength of the test piece shall not exceed +25 per cent.
After the dry heat exposure, the change in ultimate elongation of the test piece shall not exceed a maximum increase of 10 per cent and a maximum decrease of 30 per cent.

The ozone ageing test shall be in compliance with ISO 1431/1, with the test piece stressed to 20 per cent elongation and exposed to air at 40 °C with an ozone concentration of 50 parts per hundred million during 72 hours.
No cracking of the test piece is allowed after the ozone ageing test.

A non-metallic part containing liquid LPG shall comply with the leakage tests mentioned in paragraphs 5., 6. and 7. after having been submitted to a hydraulic pressure of 2.25 times the maximum operating pressure at a temperature of 120 °C during minimal 96 hours.

A non-metallic part containing liquid LPG shall comply with the leakage tests mentioned in paragraphs 5., 6. and 7. after having been submitted to a 96 hours temperature cycle from the minimum operating temperature up to the maximum operating temperature with a cycle time of 120 minutes, under maximum working pressure.

After the heat exchange fluid test, the non-metallic parts shall show a change in volume of less than 20 per cent, a change in mass of less than 5 per cent, a change in tensile strength of less than -25 per cent and a change in elongation at break within -30 per cent and +10 per cent.

All components connecting the pressure relief valve and/or the pressure relief device with the gaseous phase in the LPG container shall be tested using the procedure of paragraph 18, on two samples "a" and "b".
Sample "a" shall be aged according to paragraph 18.1.1. or 18.1.2. and the aged sample "a" shall undergo the vibration test according to paragraph 18.2.
For ageing procedure 1, the aged non-metallic materials shall comply with Annex 16, paragraph 11.2.
For ageing procedure 2, the aged component shall comply with Annex 16, paragraph 11.2.
The aged sample shall comply with the test requirements in Annex 16, paragraph 10.5., procedure A or B.
Both aged and non-aged samples "a" and "b" shall comply with the flow requirements as per paragraph 6.17.8.3. of this UN Regulation.
The non-metallic material of the samples "a" and "b" shall show no cracks, deformation or any visual damage.

Non-metallic components or parts which may come into contact with petrol shall not show excessive volume change or loss of weight, tested for resistance to petrol according to ISO 1817 with medium petrol (E10) complying with Annex 10 to UN Regulation No. 83, temperature 23 °C (tolerance according to ISO 1817) and immersion period 72 hours.
Non-metallic components and parts which may come into contact with petrol shall show a maximum change in volume of 20 per cent.

After storage in air with a temperature of 40 ºC for a period of 48 hours, the mass of non-metallic components and parts which may come into contact with petrol compared to the original value shall not decrease more than 5 per cent.
Metallic components or parts which may come into contact with petrol shall have a permanent resistance against petrol.

Metallic components or parts which may come into contact with petrol shall permanently be protected against corrosion (e.g. coating, surface finish, material mix) and fulfil the requirements of Annex 16, paragraph 12.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation.
The international approval mark shall comprise the elements given in paragraphs 5.3.1. and 5.3.2.
The international approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The international approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband limits shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band and 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2 to this Regulation.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband limits shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3 to this Regulation.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For ESAs for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude shall be +75 V.
For ESAs for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude shall be -100 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9 with test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band as given in Table 2a.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9 with the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band as given in Table 2b.

In over 90 per cent of the frequency range below 2 GHz, the ESA test level shall be 60 V/m (stripline, 20 to 400 MHz), 75 V/m (TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz), 60 mA (BCI, 20 to 400 MHz), 30 V/m (ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz) or 21 V/m (reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz), according to the method used.
In over 90 per cent of the frequency range above 2 GHz (2,000 to 6,000 MHz), the ESA test level shall be 10 V/m (ALSE) or 7 V/m (reverberation chamber); not applicable to stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

Over the whole frequency range below 2 GHz, the minimum ESA test level shall be 50 V/m (stripline, 20 to 400 MHz), 62,5 V/m (TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz), 50 mA (BCI, 20 to 400 MHz), 25 V/m (ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz) or 18 V/m (reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz), according to the method used.
Over the whole frequency range above 2 GHz (2,000 to 6,000 MHz), the minimum ESA test level shall be 8 V/m (ALSE) or 6 V/m (reverberation chamber); not applicable to stripline, TEM cell and BCI.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of ESA representative of this type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1; the starting profile is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.
Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile, the ESA immunity test level shall be II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with functional status B for immunity related functions (for ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases) or C (for other ESA), and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
For test pulse 1, the ESA immunity test level shall be -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems, with 500 pulses and FPSC III for both functions related and not related to immunity.
For test pulse 2a, the ESA immunity test level shall be +37 V for 12 V and 24 V systems, with 500 pulses and FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for not related.
For test pulse 2b, the ESA immunity test level shall be +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems, with 10 pulses and FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for not related.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA immunity test level shall be -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems, with a test duration of 1 h and FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for not related.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA immunity test level shall be +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems, with a test duration of 1 h and FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for not related.

The broadband electromagnetic emission of the ESA (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.) shall not exceed the limit E in dBµV/m at frequency F in MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth: 30-75 MHz E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz E = 63.

The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.) shall not exceed the limit E in dBµV/m at frequency F in MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth: 30-75 MHz E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz E = 53.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

ESAs may comply with any combination of (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the combination covers the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
Measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines (12/24 V supply lines).

The starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except that ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.
